Title: Thirty six thousand patients annually treated at AKUH's emergency
NewsSummary: The Aga Khan University Hospital's Section of Emergency Medicine handles 36,000 patients annually out of which 20 percent are paediatric patients and 15 percent come with cardiac problems. Section of Emergency Medicine provides care.

content.text: The Aga Khan University Hospital's Section of Emergency Medicine handles 36,000 patients annually out of which 20 percent are paediatric patients and 15 percent come with cardiac problems. Section of Emergency Medicine provides care to all types of Surgical, Medical, Obstetrical/ Gynecological, Paediatric, Psychiatric and Orthopaedic emergencies. About 60 percent of the totals are medical emergencies, similar to other emergency departments around the world.

The Head of the Section, Dr Rifat Rehmani, the only physician in Pakistan who has a Fellowship in Accident and Emergency from Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh, said that cardiac emergencies are the most common Dr Rehmani explained that the five warning signs of heart attack are prolonged pressure or squeezing pain in the center of chest or abdomen; pain spreading to or from the shoulder, neck or jaw; sweating; nausea and vomiting, and shortness of breath."Ignoring the symptoms is like playing with dynamite", added Dr Rehmani. He advised that if someone is experiencing any of these warning signs, then they should not wait but must immediately seek medical help as the first few hours after a heart attack are critical and with timely treatment many lives could be saved.

AKUH's Section of Emergency Medicine provides evaluation and treatment to patients 24- hours a day as well as 7 days a week. In addition, it provides"Triage", prioritization of patients according to medical acuity. Once a patient reaches the Emergency, he/she is greeted by a "Triage" nurse. The patients are not treated on first come first serve basis, but on their medical conditions. The Hospital has started a service for patients with minor illnesses or injuries - these patients receive prompt, efficient and high quality treatment through a "Fast Track", where they are seen and discharged within 60 minutes. This service is staffed by emergency physicians, residency-trained paediatric doctors, who have more than 10 years of experience, and specially trained and experienced nurses in Emergency Medicine are available at all times.
